info.title: Servana API — canonical v1
info.description:
The canonical Servana contract. Generated from src/api/v1/contract.ts — do not edit by hand; `npm run api:docs` rewrites it and the contract test fails if it drifts.

Operations marked `x-implemented: false` are DOCUMENTED BUT NOT MOUNTED. They exist so the legacy migration matrix can name a canonical successor before it is built, and they will 404.

Routes under /api/v1 are exempt from the cross-platform field-parity middleware that rewrites every other response, so the shapes below are exactly what the wire carries.

get.summary: The full public catalog tree: categories, their subcategories and their services.
Counts and last-updated stamp for the catalog, for cache validation.
Flat list of every bookable service, for search and deep links.
One service by its canonical services.id, including its place in the hierarchy.
get.description: Deliberately NOT status-filtered: an archived deep link resolves to an honest "unavailable" rather than a 404 dead end. `available` folds in subcategory and category status.

get.summary: The authenticated caller, whatever their role.
The caller's own bookings. Identity comes from the token, never from a parameter.
get.description: Paginated at the API boundary. The underlying service returns the whole set, so this bounds the RESPONSE, not the query — noted in the matrix as a follow-up for the bookings domain command.

get.summary: One booking, if the caller is its customer, its active provider, or an admin.
A booking's operational history, voiced for the customer.
The authenticated provider's job cards.
get.description: Three paths, one domain service. This is the clearest centralization case in the backend: two clients, two shapes, one query.

get.summary: One job card, scoped to the authenticated provider's own assignment.
The caller's notifications.
How many unread notifications the caller has.

patch.summary: Marks one notification read. Repeating it is a no-op, not an error.

post.summary: Marks every notification read. Naturally idempotent.

get.summary: A provider's published reviews. No customer identity is projected.
A provider's aggregate rating.
The caller's notification preferences.
get.description: Three legacy paths, one uid-keyed service, and two of the three are gated on a provider role for a preference table that has no role column. The role gate is the accident, not the capability.

put.summary: Replaces the caller's notification preferences. Idempotent by construction.

post.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh session.

get.summary: Cross-catalog search.
get.x-domain-service: none yet — no backend search endpoint exists
get.description: There is no backend search today. ServanaClient searches the catalog CLIENT-SIDE off the /api/services/full payload, which is why an empty level2 silently emptied the search cache. Building it belongs to the catalog/search domain command.

get.summary: The composed customer home surface.
get.description: No legacy equivalent exists. The customer home surface is assembled on the device from three or four separate calls, so there is nothing to alias — this is a new capability, and building it is a product decision about what home should contain rather than a migration. Listed here so the target architecture is complete.

get.summary: The caller's booking conversations.
The authenticated provider's earnings summary.
get.description: Money. Deliberately not adapted in a foundation command: the payout window is already documented as 48h in copy and 72h in reality, and a second read path before that is settled would give two answers to "when am I paid".

get.summary: Admin booking operations list.

firebaseIdToken.description: Verified signature AND revocation state — a token issued before a session revocation is rejected with TOKEN_REVOKED, not accepted until expiry.

message.description: Human-readable. Never branch on this — branch on `code`.

details.description: Optional structured context. Shape depends on `code`.

requestId.description: Also returned as the X-Request-Id header.

total.description: null when the total is not cheaply knowable.

lastUpdatedAt.description: ISO 8601 with a UTC designator. Never Postgres' native "2026-08-11 11:03:23.421016+00".

CatalogService.description: Never carries `level2`/`level_2`. In the legacy model those mean the SUBCATEGORY; response parity used to map `name` onto them, which made a Service claim its own name as its subcategory. /api/v1 is exempt from that middleware.

available.description: Folds in subcategory and category status. Detail is NOT status-filtered, so an archived deep link resolves to an honest "unavailable" rather than a 404.

id.description: Same value as uid. Present for clients that key on `id`.

uid.description: The Firebase uid. THE primary key — there is no numeric user id.

role.description: 1 admin, 2 and 4 provider, 3 customer. See servana_role_map.

Booking.description: A booking as produced by bookingService.formatBooking.

BookingTimeline.description: Operational history, voiced for the customer. Not the audit record (§16).

JobCard.description: A job card as produced by controllers/jobCardView.formatJobCard.

NotificationMutation.description: Outcome flags from the notification service.

NotificationPreferences.description: Per-channel preference flags, keyed by uid.

Session.description: PLANNED — owned by the auth domain command.

SearchResults.description: PLANNED — no backend search exists today.

ConversationList.description: PLANNED — owned by the messaging domain command.

EarningsSummary.description: PLANNED — owned by the provider-earnings domain command.

AdminBookingList.description: PLANNED — owned by the admin-bookings domain command.
